transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel, Samir Rao, Priya Nair, Jon Park, Eddie Liu

Summary: Quick sync to validate Q3 launch readiness for the Dedicated launch candidate. Focus on canary metrics, SLOs, automation, and docs.

[00:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone for joining, uh, we'll kick off. The goal today is to align on the Q3 launch for Dedicated, make sure canary and SLOs are in shape and that the runbooks + docs are ready. I know we have some outstanding items.

[00:18] Samir: yeah, quick note, ran the perf job last night, it looks ok for 90%ile at the baseline, but we saw a CPU spike on the batcher when sequence lengths hit 1024, so there's some KV cache thrash - well the, the K V cache, kv cache, sorry, um and that caused two pod restarts in the staging cluster.

[00:35] Priya: I saw that, the restart was because the OOM killer stepped in during the large token window. It seems related to quantization memory regen with our new 4-bit matrix. Might be a scheduling/oom threshold we need to tune.

[00:55] Eddie: yeah that aligns with the local repros I ran. Under a mixed seq length profile we get memory fragmentation on the runtime path, especially with the custom kernel switch. Might need a small allocator tweak or to force a compact between requests, which is not ideal.

[01:15] Jon: ok so action item for Eddie to add those repros and for Samir to re-run canary with the mixed profile. Also we should make sure the canary includes a tail-latency stress test, not just average tps.

[01:36] Maya: agreed. Priya, for SLOs, are we comfortable with the alert thresholds? We wanted to keep p99 under 300ms for our targeted Dedicated tier.

[01:46] Priya: current synthetic shows p99 at ~270ms in green region but in the spike windows it goes over 500ms. I'm going to add a synthetic that runs token heavy prompts with parallel requests to emulate the tail. Also adding a smoke test that exercises KV cache hits vs misses.

[02:10] Samir: question on routing - our smart routing policy, are we going to route to cheaper quantized models when latency is not sensitive? We had notes from Product to allow a degraded mode to keep throughput but reduce cost. That has implications for canary because we need to exercise fallbacks.

[02:30] Maya: yes, we want a policy in place, but for initial Dedicated launch I want deterministic behavior: primary model pinned, then a controlled fallback path. Canary should test both primary and fallback under load so we measure divergence in output quality and latency.

[02:50] Eddie: small point, the metric we measure for quality divergence - we'll need prompts and evals, maybe run our small eval harness of 200 prompts. I'll add that to the canary plan.

[03:05] Maya: good. Jon, can you confirm the automation for canary rollouts in the pipeline? We want a canary to be able to auto-scale and then either promote or rollback based on SLO windows.

[03:20] Jon: current infra has a canary controller that supports promotion, but the alerting tie-ins are manual. I can add an automated gate that reads the p95/p99 windows from Grafana, but we need to define guardrails - like allowed error rate, latency thresholds, and quality regression thresholds.

[03:40] Priya: for alerts, I also want to make sure we have a separate runbook for degraded behavior versus total outage. Degraded: increased latencies, fallbacks to quantized models - that's our graceful degradation. Outage: model serving pods down or KV cache unreachable. Different playbooks.

[04:05] Samir: noted. Also re: KV cache, we had a kb note that the incremental cache invalidation wasn't happening fast enough when we roll keys across instances. We need to either shorten TTL or use a broadcast invalidation.

[04:25] Eddie: broadcast invalidation adds network chatter; TTL of 30s might be good enough for launch. We can tune after. But for now, set TTL to 20s in canary to minimize stale hits.

[04:40] Maya: ok TTL 20s for canary. Samir to update config.

[04:50] Jon: another dependency - billing flags and quotas. The billing team needs the Dedicated SKU defined so we can throttle new accounts during rollout. Maya, can you confirm?

[05:02] Maya: yes I'll sync with Billing today. We need a tiered quota: pilot customers, GA customers, and internal test accounts.

[05:12] Priya: on the security side, Legal asked for SOC2 scoping for Dedicated and a KMS proof for customer-managed keys. Do we have the docs?

[05:23] Maya: Legal asked yesterday. I have a draft compliance checklist, but we need Security to sign off. Priya, can you coordinate and add the KMS integration steps into the install doc?

[05:32] Priya: yep I'll add steps and a note about HSM support in the private deploy path.

[05:40] Samir: performance benchmarks - I attached the sheet in the meeting notes, but takeaways: steady-state throughput looks good; cold-start memory overhead still a gap. Could that be a concern for first request latency?

[05:54] Eddie: cold-start is about initial kernel warm-up and KV cache miss; we can mitigate with a lightweight pre-warm job in our autoscaler and a small warm pool for Dedicated for the pilot. Costs a little but keeps p95 down.

[06:10] Maya: ok we will budget for a small warm pool for pilot customers. Note: add to cost model.

[06:18] Jon: docs status - are runbooks in the repo? I saw a few stale ones. We need consolidated runbook + step-by-step rollback with commands.

[06:30] Maya: Eddie and Jon, please pair on finalizing the runbook. Make sure the runbook references the playbook in Ops and has clear owners for each step.

[06:42] Eddie: will do. We'll include exact kubectl commands, canary promotion steps, and the Grafana queries for the SLO windows.

[06:55] Priya: alerting thresholds proposal: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 350ms for Dedicated baseline. If p99>500ms for more than 5 mins, auto trigger investigation and consider rollback.

[07:12] Samir: question about fallback quality - if we route to quantized model, do we notify users about quality drift? We should surface a header or a response flag so consumers can opt-in or adjust.

[07:28] Maya: yes let's add a response metadata flag for fallback mode. Engineering can add a response header like x-rd-fallback: quantized. That will let clients know and help debug.

[07:40] Jon: on the canary schedule - propose a 72-hour canary with step increases: 1% traffic, 5%, 20%, 100% inside the pilot namespace. Each step holds for 6 hours and checks SLOs.

[08:00] Priya: that seems reasonable. Need automation to stop promotion on alert. I'll add guard rails in our canary controller.

[08:12] Maya: good. Ops tickets - who is owning on-call during canary? We need a primary and secondary.

[08:20] Jon: I'll own primary for the first canary window and Priya as secondary. We'll rotate after.

[08:30] Samir: risk register quick review: outstanding items - a) memory fragmentation fix b) billing quota flags c) Legal sign-off on KMS d) docs/runbook cleanup e) cold-start warm pool.

[08:46] Maya: rank those: memory fragmentation is P0 to resolve before wider pilot; billing and legal are P1 but blocking GA; docs and warm pool P2.

[09:00] Eddie: on memory fragmentation, I have a small patch that compacts allocator after each session; it's in a branch. If it passes QA with mixed seq lengths it should cut tail-latency. I'll open a PR today.

[09:15] Priya: once PR is merged, Samir can re-run that perf job.

[09:22] Samir: yes I'll schedule it for 04/01 in staging with the mixed profile.

[09:30] Maya: perfect. A few notes: Marketing wants a short blurb for the pilot announcement - but let's wait until Legal signs the compliance checklist. Also, we need an internal all-hands note for the launch prep on the morning of rollout.

[09:45] Jon: I'll draft the internal note and share the timeline.

[09:50] Maya: ok quick recap of decisions: TTL 20s for KV cache in canary, warm pool for pilot, automated canary gate tied to p95/p99 + quality eval, fallback flag header x-rd-fallback, on-call primary is Jon, PR for memory compaction is top priority.

[10:10] Samir: any blockers from infra side? We need an extra GPU pool for pilot customers. I put a request in the infra queue but will escalate if needed.

[10:22] Maya: escalate and cc me.

[10:30] Priya: security note - I'll circulate the KMS integration doc by end of day and request Security review.

[10:35] Eddie: small transcribe glitch - we also discussed model quantization edge cases; will attach the test cases to the canary plan.

[10:45] Maya: great, thanks. Let's capture action items and owners. We'll meet again after first canary run.

[10:55] Jon: can we do a quick 10-min sync next Thursday to review canary results?

[11:00] Maya: scheduling now. Thanks everyone. End.

Notes on transcription: some speaker attribution may be imperfect; product names sometimes transcribed as 'Dedicate' or 'Redwood Dedicate' or 'K V cache'. References to external docs: canary benchmark spreadsheet (link in meeting notes), runbook PR (link), compliance checklist (link).
